This section was checked against exported VBA at commit
`3b4c05386e5a44d05633136ecbcf5dd067f70435`. The retained technical draft was
used as a coverage checklist, not as proof of behaviour. Static source review
does not replace testing in Excel with a supported database and representative,
non-production workbooks.
:::

## Purpose and audience

NADABAS is an Excel add-in implemented in Visual Basic for Applications (VBA).
It coordinates data movement between Excel workbooks and configured databases,
and provides workbook, classification, correspondence, batch, document, and
administrative workflows.

These pages are intended for maintainers, reviewers, database administrators,
security reviewers, and developers preparing a gradual migration. Familiarity
with Excel and basic VBA is assumed. Installation and ordinary end-user
instructions belong in separate guides.

## Evidence labels

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Source-verified** | Directly supported by exported source at the baseline commit. Runtime behaviour may still require testing. |
| **Environment-dependent** | Implemented in source, but the outcome depends on Office, Windows, drivers, database configuration, permissions, or files. |
| **Legacy-draft** | Present in the retained draft but not established by the current source. |
| **Unknown** | Evidence is insufficient; do not treat the statement as established behaviour. |

## System map

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  user["User or administrator"]
  subgraph excel["Microsoft Excel process"]
    ribbon["Ribbon and UserForms"]
    events["Application events"]
    commands["Command and workflow modules"]
    model["Globals and class modules"]
    workbook["Workbook named ranges and cells"]
    access["ADO and ADOX data access"]
  end
  registry[("Windows user registry")]
  database[("Base, exchange, or satellite database")]
  files[("Local or shared files")]

  user --> ribbon
  ribbon --> commands
  events --> commands
  commands <--> workbook
  commands <--> model
  commands --> access
  access <--> database
  model <--> registry
  commands <--> files
```

**Diagram description.** Ribbon callbacks and Excel events invoke command
modules. Commands inspect workbook named ranges, coordinate session and domain
objects, and use ADO/ADOX-based routines to access configured databases. The
Windows registry and file system are external trust boundaries.

## Source layout

At the baseline commit the export contains 78 standard modules, 41 class
modules, and 66 UserForms with 66 matching binary `.frx` resources.

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `vba/modules/` | Startup, ribbon callbacks, commands, validation, data access, and operating-system interfaces. |
| `vba/classes/` | Database, workbook, domain, settings, permission, scan-result, and tree-view objects. |
| `vba/forms/` | UserForms (`.frm`) and their binary resources (`.frx`). |

The files below `vba/` are the version-controlled source of truth. An `.xlam` or
`.xlsm` file is a build or release artifact and must not be used to silently
overwrite reviewed source.

## Reading path

1. [Lifecycle and user interface](lifecycle-and-ui.qmd) explains startup,
   events, ribbon state, forms, and global session state.
2. [Workbooks and data movement](workbooks-and-data.qmd) explains registration,
   portable paths, named ranges, validation, load/save, and documents.
3. [Database access and schema](database-access.qmd) explains database roles,
   registry settings, ADO/ADOX, SQL helpers, and source-defined tables.
4. [Domain workflows and administration](domain-and-administration.qmd) covers
   classifications, correspondences, key families, batches, design, backup,
   settings, conversion, and debugging.
5. [Localization and component reference](localization-and-components.qmd)
   covers translated UI resources, component conventions, and review risks.
6. [Legacy draft coverage](legacy-draft-coverage.qmd) accounts for every major
   section of the retained draft and records deferred claims.

## Maintenance rules

- Update implementation text and source links in the same pull request as a
  relevant VBA change.
- Keep exact identifiers, table names, range names, and procedure names in
  their source casing, including existing spelling inconsistencies.
- Record environment evidence separately from static source evidence.
- Never copy registry values, credentials, production paths, or statistical
  data into documentation or review artifacts.
- Prefer a small issue or ADR to an unowned `TODO`, `+++`, or diagram
  placeholder in published documentation.

## Gradual migration seam

These pages describe the current VBA boundary so functionality can be replaced
incrementally. A safe .NET migration can introduce one tested seam at a time
while Excel/VBA remains the operational fallback. Candidate seams include
schema inspection, configuration validation, SQL construction, logging, and
batch orchestration. Behaviour should first be characterized against this
baseline and representative workbooks; a rewrite must not infer requirements
from undocumented VBA side effects.
